Shortlist Luxon only if its documented purpose matches your use case; the source signals below are context, not an endorsement.

Best fit — and when to skip it

Luxon is most relevant to developers working with JavaScript/TypeScript. Its source topics point to date, immutable. It belongs on a shortlist when that stated purpose matches a concrete requirement.

Skip or postpone it when the documented runtime, license, dependency footprint, or maintenance model conflicts with your project. Popularity alone is not a reason to migrate.

Setup and first checks

Confirm the exact package name, current version, runtime requirement, dependencies, provenance, and release notes before installing luxon in a production project. Start in a disposable example and exercise the use case you actually need.

Maintenance and risk signals

The collected source record shows 35.9M weekly downloads, version 3.7.2, and released 2025-09-05.

The recorded Node.js requirement is >=12.

The registry lists 2 maintainers.

The source reports the MIT license.

Registry downloads include automated requests and are not unique users, satisfaction, or proof of quality.

Bottom line

Luxon is worth a closer look when its stated purpose and ecosystem fit your project. Compare it with related tools, verify the current documentation, and test the smallest realistic use case before committing.

Try it safely

npm install luxon
